context: Linked scatterplot matrix (SPLOM) of iris-like synthetic data with 4 variables and 3 species; KDE density plots on the diagonal update on brush selection across all cells.
first_impression: Well-engineered SPLOM with honest encoding throughout: data-driven scale domains, principled KDE bandwidth, and no area/size deception.
what_works: Silverman's rule used for KDE bandwidth (data-driven, not arbitrary); all scatter and density scale domains derived from d3.extent(data) rather than hardcoded magic numbers.
what_doesnt: Scatter joins use .data(data).join('circle') without a key function, making the visualization index-dependent and fragile under data reordering (permutation robustness failure); yDensity scale is fixed from full-data maxD and not recalculated when brush subset changes, which can cause brushed density curves to appear visually flat for small subsets.
